title: PTY Stream Backpressure & Process-Tree Lifecycle Architecture
objective: Investigate, architect, and benchmark safe PTY stream write backpressure, Windows taskkill/tree-kill child process cleanup, and IPC burst throughput safeguards without breaking existing contracts.
context: High-volume terminal output bursts (e.g. cat of 100k lines or build logs) can overwhelm the Electron IPC bridge and cause UI freezes or memory bloat. Furthermore, child process trees on Windows must be killed cleanly on terminal session closure.
expected_deliverables: Security analysis of IPC buffer limits and denial-of-service risks
Performance analysis comparing high-water-mark chunking vs unthrottled streaming
Windows process-tree cleanup specification using native taskkill flags or tree-kill helper
Draft IPC schema changes for proposed terminal stream flow-control
acceptance_criteria: Zero unhandled buffer overflows under 50MB burst streams
Zero orphaned child processes (node, bash, python) when session closes
Conforms to Ponytail simplicity ladder (stdlib/native first, no new unvetted npm packages)

risk_assessment.mitigation: Isolate buffer queueing logic in main process service; preserve existing terminal:data event contract
